articles.headline: Riggs Evaluates Nitro Motorsports Future as Offseason Begins
articles.dek: Samuel Riggs and Nitro Motorsports continue discussions regarding equipment struggles following the conclusion of the 2026 schedule.
articles.body:
The conclusion of the racing calendar brings contract discussions to the forefront for several competitors across the garage. Samuel Riggs finds himself evaluating equipment performance following a challenging run through the twenty-six events. Riggs enters the final year of his current agreement with Nitro Motorsports, which concludes at the end of this campaign.

Sources close to the team indicate that talks between management and the driver remain active as both parties assess potential directions for the upcoming year. Performance metrics from the recent events have prompted a thorough review of preparation methods within the shop. Nitro Motorsports aims to address speed deficits before the next season commences.

Other garage members face different contract situations as the garage closes its doors for the winter months. Several top drivers finished their current agreements following the Kansas event, opening discussions for upcoming team alignments. Official announcements regarding crew chief assignments and car number modifications are expected as winter testing approaches.

articles.headline: Analyzing Midfield Charges and Final Speeds at Kansas Speedway
articles.dek: A look at the numbers behind the season finale at Kansas Speedway, highlighting impressive climbs through the field and the final standings.
articles.body:
The final round of the twenty-six race schedule concluded at Kansas Speedway with forty-one completed circuits. Teams faced clear skies and cool temperatures at forty-five degrees Fahrenheit alongside a southeast wind blowing at ten miles per hour. Three yellow flags slowed the field during the afternoon.

McCoy Behnke delivered a strong performance by advancing from seventeenth on the grid to secure the runner-up position at the finish line. Behnke spent sixteen circuits leading the pack before settling behind the race winner. Scott Chegg executed the largest upward movement of the day. Starting thirty-first, Chegg worked his way forward to cross the finish line in eighth position.

Nick Apollo moved from fifteenth to fourth by the checkered flag, guiding his machine through eight circuits at the front. Johnathan Langley drove from twelfth to fifth without leading a lap. Tyler Raheem gained five positions from his eleventh starting spot to finish sixth.

King Robinson concluded the campaign with the overall points title, accumulating thirty-one hundred twenty-seven markers and three victories. Nicholas Hoggeton secured second in the final rundown with thirty--two hundred nine markers and three wins. James Baker claimed third overall with twenty-eight hundred sixty-eight markers alongside three triumphs.

articles.headline: James Baker Closes ARCA Season With Kansas Victory
articles.dek: James Baker drove to victory in the season-ending Menards 150 at Kansas Speedway, while King Robinson secured the overall championship.
articles.body:
James Baker captured the win in the final round of the simulation season, taking the checkered flag by 3.856 seconds in the Menards 150 at Kansas Speedway. Baker drove the number 18 machine from eighth on the grid to lead 11 laps, outrunning a 32-car field on the 1.5-mile intermediate oval.

McCoy Behnke finished in the runner-up spot after charging 15 positions from seventeenth on the starting grid, pacing the field for 16 laps. George Noble rounded out the podium in third place after leading four circuits. Nick Apollo came home fourth and Johnathan Langley completed the top five.

The race featured three caution periods and six lead changes among five different drivers under clear skies and a chilly 45-degree ambient temperature. Pole sitter Dallas Underwood led two laps before fading to ninth at the finish. Scott Chegg earned hard charger recognition by advancing 23 positions from thirty-first to eighth.

King Robinson officially claimed the 2026 title with 3127 points and three victories. Nicholas Hoggeton finished second in the final standings with 3029 points and three wins, followed by Baker in third with 2868 points and three wins. Daniel Stavchanksy and Karson Mitchell rounded out the top five in the season-long standings.

The series now enters the offseason, giving teams time to prepare for the upcoming simulation calendar.

articles.headline: Analyzing the Title Math and Win Probabilities for Kansas
articles.dek: King Robinson holds a narrow advantage heading into the season finale at Kansas Speedway, but simulator projections give Nicholas Hoggeton a slight edge in win probability.
articles.body:
The championship battle in the sim league comes down to the final event of the 2026 schedule at Kansas Speedway. King Robinson leads the standings with 3015 points and three victories. His closest challenger, Nicholas Hoggeton, sits just 77 points behind at 2938 points, also holding three wins.

Mathematically, the title fight is a two-driver duel between Robinson and Hoggeton. James Baker occupies third place in the standings with 2688 points and two wins, mathematically eliminated from overtaking the top spot given the maximum points available in a single event. Daniel Stavchanksy holds fourth with 2620 points, followed by Karson Mitchell in fifth with 2607 points and Kolby Newman in sixth with 2596 points.

Looking ahead to the intermediate layout at Kansas, the simulator model views the championship rivals as co-favorites. Nicholas Hoggeton enters with a model win probability of 28 percent, reflecting his recent momentum after controlling the race at Bristol. King Robinson follows closely with a 27 percent win probability.

Further down the projection sheet, James Baker sits at 13 percent, Daniel Dominguez at nine percent, Daniel Stavchanksy at eight percent, and Kolby Newman at four percent. Robinson needs a steady run to lock up the crown, while Hoggeton likely requires a victory and assistance from misfortune striking the leading car to erase the 77-point deficit.

articles.headline: Hoggeton Dominates Bristol to Close Gap as Title Finale Looms
articles.dek: Nicholas Hoggeton drove his way to a dominant win at Bristol Motor Speedway, setting up a high-stakes championship showdown in the final race of the season.
articles.body:
Nicholas Hoggeton put on a clinic at Bristol Motor Speedway during the Bush's Beans 200, pacing the field for 162 laps to secure his third victory of the sim-racing campaign. Hoggeton started fifth in the thirty-two machine field and controlled the tempo through seven caution periods, crossing the stripe 1.264 seconds ahead of Karson Mitchell.

Mitchell chased the leader hard after starting sixth, logging thirty circuits at the front and finishing runner-up. Caleb Guerrier took third following an eleventh-place start, while McCoy Behnke and Tyler Payne rounded out the top five. Championship leader King Robinson salvaged a sixth-place result after climbing fifteen positions from his twenty-first starting slot, keeping a grip on the standings lead heading into the season finale.

Attrition factored heavily on the concrete bullring. Nick Apollo bowed out due to suspension trouble, Atsz Minyoung suffered a transmission failure, and Ryan Davis exited early following an on-track collision. Further back, Caden Everett charged through the pack from thirty-first to seventh, earning the hard charger honors of the afternoon.

King Robinson commands the standings with 3015 markers and three triumphs. Nicholas Hoggeton sits right behind with 2938 counters, also holding three wins as the championship battle reaches its final round.

The series shifts focus to the twentieth and final event of the season, where the championship will officially be decided between the top contenders.

articles.headline: Stavchanksy Ends Drought with North Wilkesboro Victory
articles.dek: Daniel Stavchanksy drove from pole to victory lane in race seventeen, snapping a twelve-race winless skid.
articles.body:
Daniel Stavchanksy broke a long dry spell on Sunday afternoon at North Wilkesboro Speedway, converting his pole position into a dominant win at the Audubon Park 100. Stavchanksy paced the field for 89 circuits, managing nine caution periods and holding off late charges to secure his second victory of the 2026 season by 0.747 seconds.

King Robinson pushed hard from the fourth starting spot, leading 46 laps before settling for the runner-up slot. Alfie Denley delivered the performance of the afternoon, carving through traffic after starting 26th to claim the final step of the podium while also pacing 42 circuits. McCoy Behnke advanced from 17th to fourth, and George Noble rounded out the leading group after commanding the asphalt for 28 laps.

Attrition heavily influenced the 300-lap affair. Mechanical failures sidelined William Faison, Valdemar Estriden, and Atsz Minyoung with transmission issues, while Brenden Gregg exited due to a heavy crash. The resulting yellows kept the field bunched and forced crew chiefs into strategic tire conservation and fuel preservation choices.

With only three events remaining before the championship battle concludes, the standings picture grows tighter. King Robinson maintains control at the summit with 2690 points and three victories, followed by Nicholas Hoggeton holding 2568 tallies. James Baker sits third with 2432 markers, while Stavchanksy's triumph solidifies his fourth-place position at 2343 points.

The tour shifts focus onward as the remaining schedule dwindles down.

George Noble capitalized on absolute chaos on the final lap to win the General Tire 200 at Daytona International Speedway. Julian Paxton ended up upside down on his roof as the smoke cleared, while thirty-one of the thirty-two starting entries sustained damage in the massive melee.

Vincent Crook navigated the early laps cleanly to secure runner-up honors, while Dallas Underwood drove a steady race from thirteenth on the grid to claim third place. Daniel Stavchanksy pulled off the biggest advance of the afternoon, surging twenty-one spots from twenty-eighth to finish seventh.

Aaron Kyan put his machine on the pole for the General Tire 200, but the front row failed to dictate the outcome of the 20-lap superspeedway sprint. Kyan tumbled down the running order to finish 16th, leaving the top spot vacant for drivers lurking further back in the 32-car field.

George Noble provided the ultimate proof of the starting position irrelevance. Starting 19th, Noble avoided trouble during the race's lone caution period and picked his way to the front to claim his first career victory by a margin of 2.970 seconds. He was not alone in making a significant climb. Vincent Crook advanced from 11th to finish second, while Dallas Underwood converted a 13th-place start into a podium finish in third.

The most dramatic charge of the afternoon came from Daniel Stavchanksy. Lined up 28th on the grid, Stavchanksy used the draft to methodically pick off opponents over the 20 laps, ultimately crossing the stripe in seventh to earn the biggest mover honors of the day. Similarly, McCoy Behnke climbed from 20th to eighth, and John Verstappen moved from 21st to ninth.

Pack racing dynamics on superspeedways consistently neutralize qualifying advantages. Drivers who conserve equipment and maintain track position during the draft frequently outlast those who lead early laps. With 18 races remaining before the series shifts focus later in the year, the Daytona opener suggests that adaptability in traffic outweighs raw qualifying pace.
